title: Amazon White Background Photo Guide | AIVideosUGC
description: Make an Amazon white background main image from a phone photo: pure white RGB 255, product filling 85% or more of the frame, nothing extra added on top.
h1: How to Make an Amazon White Background Photo for Your Main Image
lead: An Amazon white background photo is a square main image on pure white, with the real product filling at least 85% of the frame and nothing extra drawn on top.
summary: Make the main image pure white, keep only what you ship, fill most of the square, and check the result against the item in your hand.

sections.h2: What are the Amazon main image requirements?
paras: The main image needs a pure white background, the product you actually sell, and no text, badges, or props that do not come in the box.

Amazon's product image guidance asks for pure white, RGB 255, 255, 255, and for the product to fill 85% or more of the frame. Only the item being sold should appear. The same guidance asks for a longest side of 500 pixels or more, 1,000 or more when you want zoom, and no side longer than 10,000 pixels. Clothing and jewelry listings can add further rules, so read the current Seller Central guide for your category before you upload.

sections.h2: Does my phone photo already need a white background?
paras: No. It needs the whole product, in focus, with even light and a little space around every edge.

Shoot near a window on a plain surface and hold the phone at the product's height. Show what the buyer finds in the box. If two lids ship with the bottle, both lids belong in the photo. If a strap is sold separately, leave it out.

sections.h2: How do I make a pure white background product photo?
paras: Upload a clear photo of the whole product and ask for that same item on pure white, including every piece that ships with it.

Open the [AI product background changer](page:change-background) or the [AI product photo generator](page:photo-hub), then write one plain line such as "the bottle and both lids on pure white." The old backdrop comes off, and the field behind the product is set to pure white. The result is square, which suits a main image. One image uses 24 credits, shown before you confirm. A failed job returns those credits. The finished file is yours to use commercially and has no watermark.

sections.h2: What Amazon product photo rules should I verify before upload?
paras: Sample the corners with a color picker, then set the real product next to the screen and compare shape, color, parts, and label.

Each sampled spot should read pure white, with no gray haze. Zoom in on labels, because small lettering is where a new image tends to drift. If the words are wrong, try again from a sharper source photo. Also check the size in the square. A tiny product in a wide white field looks small beside listings that fill the frame.
sections.alt: Adult hands compare an olive canvas backpack with a blank white square card.

sections.h2: What if the product is white, clear, or a set?
paras: Shape the item first, light the edges, and show exactly the number of pieces the listing sells.

A white product can disappear on white. Shoot the source with light from one side so the outline has soft shading, and mention gentle side light in the line you type. Clear glass picks up the room behind it, so photograph it against a plain light wall. A three-pack should show three units, not two and not five. Fluff bags and soft goods before the source shot, because the new image follows the shape it sees.
sections.alt: Adult hand shapes an olive canvas backpack upright on a white sweep.

sections.h2: Should a white background for product listings cover every image?
paras: No. Keep the white rules on the main image only, and use the later slots for use, scale, and detail.

A useful set might show the bottle in a gym bag, a hand for scale, and a close view of the lid seal. Make the pictures first, then add any words in your own editor. A soft shadow, if you want one, belongs on a later image, not on the pure-white main image. The same white main image can also lead the product page on your own store, so shoppers see one look in both places. For scenes that are not the main image, [AI lifestyle product photos](page:lifestyle-photos) are the separate job.

faq.q: Why does my white background look gray on Amazon?
faq.a: Part of the backdrop is probably not fully white, often near a corner or under the product. Sample a few spots. If they read off-white, make another version or brighten the backdrop in an editor before you upload.

faq.q: Can an AI-made photo be my Amazon main image?
faq.a: Yes, when it shows the product a buyer will receive. Match shape, color, parts, and label before it goes live. The file is yours to use commercially and has no watermark. Category rules can change, so read the current Seller Central guide for your category before you upload.

faq.q: How do I verify the white before I upload?
faq.a: Confirm pure white at RGB 255, 255, 255, no extra props, and the product filling at least 85% of the frame.

faq.q: How many credits does one white image use?
faq.a: One image uses 24 credits. The cost appears before you start, and a failed job returns the credits.
Compare the result with the real item. If the shape, color, or part count drifted, do not upload that file. Run it again from a sharper photo.

faq.q: Which Amazon product photo rules sit outside the main image?
faq.a: Later images can show use, scale, and detail. Keep prices and badges out of the picture and add those words yourself. Category rules for clothing and jewelry can be stricter, so check the current guide for your category.

faq.q: What if my Amazon main image breaks the rules?
faq.a: Replace it. A main image that breaks the white, size, or product rules can come off the listing, and the listing can drop out of search until the image is fixed. Later photos can show the product in use. Read the current Seller Central guide for your category before you upload again.

faq.q: What size should the Amazon file be?
faq.a: Amazon's published guidance asks for a longest side of 500 pixels or more, 1,000 or more when you want zoom, and no side longer than 10,000 pixels. The picture should still show the real product.

faq.q: Can I run the white backdrop across many SKUs?

faq.q: Can the API make the main image?
faq.a: Yes. Point it at the same pure-white setup you use by hand, including only what ships in the box.
